registration.note: The June 2025 leaf-on laser's near-ground intensity is too smooth over Norrfällsviken's open ground for the raw correlation: 2 and 3 patches of 111 and 74 were accepted, most peaks flat or on the search border. With both images high-passed (6 m; 1.5 m and 3 m gave the same shift for 2024 within 0.05 m) 19 (2024) and 11 (2020) laser patches are accepted, and the two photos agree on 37 (bright) and 40 (red) patches; the loop closes within 0.15 m (2024 minus 2020 against the laser 0.36 E, 0.17 N; photo against photo 0.48 E, 0.08 N). The owner accepted the direct laser shifts below 30 patches on 2026-11-09.

rounds.note: round 1: the type-aware detector tuned from TYPED_DEFAULTS; one sample for all four rounds (reference-windows.json, carried verbatim by rounds r2-r4): calibration C1-C11, held-out H1-H6, frozen on 2026-11-09 before any detector ran; tuned in order on calibration only, and scored once, all four locks together, in round r4's benchmark under the rule declared in reference-windows.json
round 2: the refined detector (r1's settings; a suppressed top taken back only on its own laser cone and apex and a separate crown in the photo); the same sample

round 3: the fused detector (r2's lock, then suppressed laser tops a learned photo crown confirms: DeepForest on the June 2024 photo, matched in photo space after the relief displacement; the photo never places a tree); the same sample

round 4: the width split extending r3 (suppressed laser tops taken back inside crowns too wide for one tree of their height, never on a mapped building), Johannesberg's round 6; the same sample, and the round whose benchmark scores all four locks once. Scored once on 2026-11-09 on H1-H6 (112 crowns), all four locks together: r1 typed P 0.938 R 0.938 F1 0.938, r2 refined 0.921 / 0.938 / 0.929, r3 fused 0.929 / 0.938 / 0.933, r4 split 0.929 / 0.938 / 0.933 (the published trees of 2026-09-04 with their stands 0.854 / 0.366 / 0.513). Under the rule declared in reference-windows.json the highest held-out F1 wins and none is passed over for precision (the best is r1's own 0.938), so this round publishes the round-1 lock (publishes: r1); it passes the 90% gate outright

photoDetect.$comment: The learned crown detector on the June 2024 photo (rounds r3, r4), run by --stage photo-detect on the GPU as at Johannesberg: DeepForest (weecology, MIT licence) through photo/crowns.py; pretrained sources at several patch sizes and fine-tuned sources cross-fitted on the two calibration folds. The fused tuning chooses one source and the fusion settings on calibration only.

r4.$comment: main session, 2026-11-09: round 4 keeps the round-3 lock and searches only the width split, with excludeBuildings fixed on, on calibration, on the whole-window detections the score reads; the best calibration F1 among settings whose calibration precision is at least the round-3 lock's on the same windows (Johannesberg round 6's tuning).

typeRule.note: Johannesberg's rule (a broadleaf call needs a clearly leafless leaf-off crown), its threshold set the same way: below every reference conifer. The 22 May 2020 photo was flown as the birches came into leaf: 15 of the 16 reference broadleaves read vegetated there (shares 0.36-1.00; one at 0.13), and two reference conifers lie below 0.2 (an 18 m crown shaded in the closed wood C3 at 0.09, a 5 m pine at 0.15). At 0.2 the rule would call one broadleaf right and two conifers wrong; at 0.08 it calls none of the reference crowns broadleaf. So this photo gives (almost) no broadleaf calls: unknown records and the stand fill take the engine's conifer-led background mix, and garden birches are drawn by that mix. The fitted rule (type-rule.json, aprilVegetatedShare >= 0.739 conifer) reaches balanced accuracy 0.83 on calibration but 0.51 on the five held-out broadleaves. For the owner's species check (main session, 2026-11-09). Spot check of all 22 broadleaf calls on the photos (main session, 2026-11-09): about 10 broadleaves (birch and bushes, bare in May 2020 and green in June 2024), 6 small pines in deep shadow (dark in both photos: May 2020 share 0-0.024, June 2024 share 0-0.028), 2 roofs of houses the map lacks and 4 unclear; both calls near play were wrong (a pine and a roof). The leaf-off share cannot tell them apart (all below 0.025), the June share can: every broadleaf there is 0.27-1.0 and every pine below 0.03, so a broadleaf call also needs a crown in leaf in June 2024 (broadleafMinimumPresenceShare 0.15, the no-vegetation hold's own threshold).

bank.note: Johannesberg's bank rule (round 5): a crown centroid over mapped water, a path, a road or a played surface gets a stem on its own laser crown's land side, never on a building

holds.note: the pole-like hold and the bank rule as at Johannesberg; held crowns are decided on the photo chips

publication.reviewStatement: reviewed candidates, review-2026-11-09 round r4, publishing the round-1 lock under the rule declared before scoring: the type-aware laser detector (June 2025 leaf-on scan) tuned on calibration windows C1-C11, scored once with the refined, fused and split detectors on the unseen sample H1-H6 (112 crowns): P 0.938 / R 0.938, held-out gate passed; agent-led reference interpretation, not a survey; crowns leaning over mapped water, paths, roads and played surfaces given a stem on the bank inside their own laser crown (holds.bank); crowns held on buildings or without June 2024 vegetation decided on the photos (hold-review.json: roofs, sheds, decks and caravans not placed); broadleaf only where the May 2020 crown is bare and the June 2024 crown in leaf; holds, removals and unresolved cases listed in the review

ownerDecisions.decision: Photo registration: "Apply measured shifts (Recommended)": the high-passed direct laser shifts are applied although they rest on fewer than 30 patches (registration.ownerAccepted).

Publication: after the before/after screenshots taken on his GPU at his request ("Grab some screenshots"), the owner answered "Commit and merge to main in the recommended way". The round-4 benchmark passes the held-out gate on the round-1 lock, so no exception is needed; the trees were staged with --pending-owner, adopted into the public root and the course's prepared data re-baked. His checklist items (the not-placed list, the species mix in screenshots, the runtime cost) stay open for him to mark.
